questions.question_text: Which of the following scheduling algorithms is non-preemptive?
questions.explanation: First-Come, First-Served is strictly non-preemptive because once a process gets the CPU, it runs to completion or until it blocks for I/O.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a router in a computer network?
options: Forwarding data packets between computer networks
Amplifying network signals over long distances
Connecting hosts within the same local area network
Translating domain names to IP addresses
questions.explanation: A router operates at the network layer (Layer 3) and directs traffic between different independent networks.

questions.question_text: In relational databases, what does ACID stand for?
questions.explanation: ACID properties ensure reliable processing of database transactions.

questions.question_text: Which data structure uses LIFO (Last In, First Out) ordering?
questions.explanation: A stack follows the LIFO principle where the last element inserted is the first one to be removed.

questions.question_text: Which protocol is primarily used for secure communication over a computer network, notably the Internet?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) uses SSL/TLS protocols to encrypt communication for secure web browsing.

questions.question_text: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end communication, reliability, and flow control?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) manages end-to-end message delivery, error recovery, and flow control between hosts.

questions.question_text: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort when a poor pivot is consistently chosen?
questions.explanation: When the pivot divides the array into the most unequal partitions possible repeatedly, QuickSort degrades to quadratic time complexity O(n^2).

questions.question_text: Which memory management scheme allocates physical memory in fixed-size blocks called frames?
questions.explanation: Paging divides logical memory into blocks called pages and physical memory into fixed-size blocks called frames to eliminate external fragmentation.

questions.question_text: Which normal form in relational databases eliminates transitive dependencies for non-key attributes?
questions.explanation: A relation is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and no non-key attribute is transitively dependent on the primary key.

questions.question_text: What does the 'P' stand for in HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTPS stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure, which encrypts HTTP traffic using TLS/SSL.

questions.question_text: Which design pattern ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it?
questions.explanation: The Singleton pattern restricts object instantiation to a single instance, which is useful when exactly one object is needed.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of an index in a relational database management system?
options: To speed up data retrieval operations
questions.explanation: Indexes are data structures (like B-trees) created on columns to allow the database engine to find rows faster without scanning the entire table.

questions.question_text: Which concurrency control problem occurs when two transactions read the same data and one updates it, leading to the first transaction's update being overwritten?
questions.explanation: A lost update anomaly happens when concurrent transactions write data, causing one write to overwrite and destroy the other.

questions.question_text: Which of the following data structures is typically used to implement recursion?
questions.explanation: Recursion relies on a call stack to keep track of active subroutines and local variables.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a translator such as a compiler?
options: To convert high-level source code into machine code
questions.explanation: A compiler translates human-readable high-level programming language code into executable machine instructions.

questions.question_text: Which network topology connects all devices to a central hub or switch?
questions.explanation: In a star topology, each device is connected independently to a central hub or switch.
